evals.name: mcmc_divergence_and_rhat_remediation
evals.prompt: I just ran diagnose_mmm on model 'mmm_q1_fit' and it returned decision_status='rejected' with 18 divergences and a max R-hat of 1.08 on the tv_spend saturation parameter. What should I do to fix this model?
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies that the model is rejected due to severe divergences (>5) and high R-hat (>1.05). It explains that the leapfrog integrator is failing in the saturation parameter space. It recommends refitting with higher target_accept (0.95 or 0.98), increasing warmup tune to 2000, and simplifying or tightening the saturation prior on tv_spend.

assertions.text: agent recognizes rejected decision status and refuses to run downstream decision tools on this model
assertions.evidence: Agent states model is invalid for optimization/decisions until remediated

assertions.text: agent provides specific sampler remediation: increase target_accept to 0.95+ and increase tune iterations
assertions.evidence: Remediation includes target_accept and tune adjustments

assertions.text: agent explains the why behind divergences and high R-hat
assertions.evidence: Explains leapfrog integrator curvature and chain non-convergence

evals.name: model_selection_and_pareto_k_interpretation
evals.prompt: We fitted three alternative MMMs on the same dataset ('mmm_geom', 'mmm_delayed', 'mmm_weibull'). How should we select the best one, and what should we check if Pareto k warnings appear?
evals.expected_output: The agent recommends calling select_best_model with method='all' to compute PSIS-LOO, WAIC, and stacking weights. It explains that Pareto k > 0.7 indicates unreliable importance sampling for outlier observations and guides the user on interpreting stacking weights for Bayesian Model Averaging.

assertions.text: agent recommends calling select_best_model tool with candidate model IDs
agent explains Pareto k threshold of 0.7 and stacking weights for model averaging
assertions.evidence: Mentions k > 0.7 warning significance and BMA weights
